title: Blue Marble (2002): Clouds
credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Image by Reto Stöckli; enhancements by Robert Simmon.

source_dates.cloud_observations: Composite of two days of visible-light imagery and a third day of thermal-infrared imagery over the poles; specific observation dates are not asserted.
source_dates.note: The server modification date is not an observation date.

asset_type: Global equirectangular cloud-only display map; grayscale-looking RGB JPEG with a dark background and no alpha channel
local_transformations: None: original official NASA JPEG bytes copied without cropping, resizing, re-encoding or color changes.
recommended_use: Optional static visual cloud layer in the Explorer, using the same equirectangular UV as the Earth surface map. Dark pixels can be made transparent and lighter pixels used for white clouds as a display approximation. Do not animate the weather pattern.
appearance_limits: Fixed historical composite, not live weather or clouds at the selected UTC.
The RGB luminance is display imagery, not a calibrated cloud optical depth, probability, height or transmission measurement.
The cloud texture contributes to appearance only; it must not change Sun/Earth geometry, terrain horizons, visibility results or radio-link claims.
Some polar cloud coverage derives from thermal infrared observations, even though the result is a monochrome display layer.

cost.note: Encoded file size and dimensions only; no network-loading time, rendering-performance or device-memory benchmark has been performed.

rights.statement: NASA Earth Observatory makes this Blue Marble collection freely available for education, science, museums and public use. Retain the credit and follow NASA media usage guidelines; no endorsement is implied.
